_help: Per commodity, an indicator->1-5 map (5 = bullish). A bare number or {"score": n, "note": "why"} for auditability. Unset = held at neutral and excluded from the average, exactly like fundamentals_manual. Refreshed by the fx-strength-desk-daily task, step 2c.

Real yield direction.note: Turned bearish on the 4 Sep jobs report - payrolls beat sharply (+162k vs +56k expected, unemployment steady at 4.1%), pushing September Fed hike odds to ~63% and the 10-year yield up to 4.77-4.80%, its high for the move. Reverses the 3 Sep ADP-driven dip.

US dollar direction.note: DXY jumped on the strong 4 Sep payrolls print (+0.17% to a 99.39 high) on revived hike bets, reversing the 3 Sep ADP-driven softness. Mildly bearish gold into the 10-11 Sep CPI test.

Central-bank & ETF demand.note: Central banks bought 6.4x more gold than ETF investors sold in Q2 2026; WGC survey shows the strongest stated buying intention since 2019; ECB says gold has passed US Treasuries as the largest reserve asset (27% of holdings). Western ETF outflows are the one offset, so 4 not higher.

Safe-haven bid.note: Live escalation - the US struck Iran 1 Sep and Iran retaliated - and gold is now converting it into a bid rather than being overwhelmed by the rates channel: bounced from 4348 (1 Sep) to 4482, about +3%.

Real yield direction.note: Same reversal as gold - the strong 4 Sep payrolls beat (+162k vs +56k expected) pushed the 10-year to 4.77-4.80% and hike odds to ~63%, reversing the 3 Sep ADP-driven dip. Silver is more leveraged to the move, so the drag is felt at least as much here.

US dollar direction.note: DXY popped on the strong 4 Sep jobs print (+0.17%, 99.39 high), reversing the 3 Sep ADP-driven softness. Mildly bearish silver.

Industrial demand.note: Structural solar/electronics demand stays firm, but 2026 global growth is slowing (IEA has oil demand contracting on trade disruption), which caps the industrial pull. Net mildly positive.

Gold-silver ratio.note: Ratio ~67.5, well below the long-run ~80 average - silver has already closed most of the gap to gold, so it is no longer cheap on this measure. Neutral for further silver outperformance.

OPEC+ supply policy.note: OPEC+ approved a small +188k bpd September hike (2 Aug), completing the rollback of the 2023 voluntary cuts, then signalled quotas held steady through year-end. Removing the 'more barrels coming' overhang is mildly supportive versus the prior path. Next review 6 Sep.

Inventory trend.note: EIA week of 21 Aug: commercial crude +0.1Mb to 428.9Mb, roughly the 5-year average; refinery runs near 98% utilisation. The mid-August import-driven build has not repeated and EIA expects stocks below the 5-year low through year-end on high exports and low imports. Neutral-to-slightly-tight, up from the earlier build-heavy read.

Demand outlook.note: IEA sees 2026 oil demand contracting (~-80 kb/d), the sharpest quarterly drop since Covid, as trade disruption hits advanced economies, Asia and the Middle East. Clearly bearish; the price spike is supply-risk driven, not demand.

Geopolitical risk premium.note: Still escalating, not de-escalating: CENTCOM's Hormuz blockade count reached 87 vessels by 4 Sep, and Israel took 'operational control' of the Ali al-Taher ridge in south Lebanon - a move Iran had warned would trigger a large-scale response. Brent ~$95 / WTI ~$92, oil on track for its biggest weekly gain since July (~8-9%). No ceasefire signal; holding at 4.5.
